findings: l.3136/l.3157: Omega_lox(Gamma) is called 'the convex domain' but is not convex: for Gamma = <gamma> it is U+(gamma) disjoint union U-(gamma) (interior_achronalDomain_eq_quadrants). The proof l.3157-3165 is valid on each Gamma-invariant convex piece, hence on Omega^+-(Lambda(Gamma)).

The printed statement l.3143-3144 is nevertheless TRUE (proved, blem_sanlox), by an argument the paper does not give: no x in U_lox(Gamma) lies in a future quadrant U+(gamma) and a past quadrant U-(gamma') (not_mem_quadrantPlus_quadrantMinus). Choose the repulsive point w of gamma^{+-1} whose direction differs from the attractive direction of gamma'; some gamma'^m x crosses the hyperplane of w (exists_lt_minkB_pow_smul, the orbit's null coordinate grows like lambda'^{-m}); then gamma^{+-n} gamma'^m x - x is timelike for n large (exists_minkQ_neg_of_sign: in the null frame of gamma, |z|^2 = 2 f(z) g(z)/<n|n'> + |v(z)|^2, f(z) ~ lambda^{-n}, g(z) -> -g(x), and the transverse part v grows at most linearly, minkQ_nullV_pow_smul_sub_le). An element of Gamma with a timelike displacement is loxodromic under Rem 8.9 (a linear parabolic displaces into J^perp, which has Q >= 0; a spacelike elliptic or tangent parabolic has Omega_g = M^n), and x is not in its achronal domain (not_minkQ_neg_of_mem_UGammaLox). Hence Omega_lox(Gamma) is contained in Omega+(Lambda(Gamma)) union Omega-(Lambda(Gamma)), both in Omega(Gamma): there are no mixed-sign components, and the paper's case analysis of linear parabolics on Omega_lox is only ever needed on the one-sided pieces.

l.3159-3163 ('the convex hull of the gamma0-orbit of x is a complete lightlike line'): replaced by an exact growth argument <n|gamma^k x> = <n|c> + <n|R^k y> + k<n|p(y)>; a point of P(gamma0) in ker p has a bounded orbit, so x must first be moved off ker p inside the open set (done).
